text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- The new rail tunnels through the Swiss Alps will be builT in steps, the lower house of parliament decided. It voted to build immediately a new rail tunnel at the Loetschberg. A new tunnel at the Gotthard, which is favoured by the eastern parts of Switzerland and Zurich, will be constructed later.
- A public referendum to protect humans from reproduction manipulation did not get the support by the upper house of parliament.

- Founded by six Swiss electric utilities, private telephone operator Diax plans to build a 1,800-km fibre optic cable network to connect large populated areas in Switzerland. Diax is currently working on an agreement with Telecom PTT, the state-owned national telefon provider, to use its infrastructure to connect the households to the fibre backbone. The Swiss telecommunication market will be liberalised on January 1, 1998.
- Swiss advertisement pages in newspapers dropped in May by 7.3 percent compared to the same month last year.
- Peter Kurzo, boss of Swiss tour operator Imholz, will leave the company. Imholz' profits were dramatically down in 1996.
- The Swiss National Bank does not fear a national referendum against the 100 million Swiss franc contribution the bank wants to make to the special fund for Holocaust victimes.
